name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
principle: The product selects a cryptographic algorithm or protocol that is broken, obsolete, risky, non-standard, or private. Attackers may break the protection and read data, modify data, forge identities, or defeat signatures.
detection_signals: Java Cipher.getInstance("DES"), Cipher.getInstance("DESede"), Cipher.getInstance("RC4"), or Cipher.getInstance("ARCFOUR")
Java MessageDigest.getInstance("MD4"), MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5"), or MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-1") used for signatures, integrity, certificates, or passwords
OpenSSL EVP_des_*(), DES_*(), RC4(), EVP_rc4(), EVP_md4(), EVP_md5(), or EVP_sha1() in security-sensitive code
Cipher transformation contains "/ECB/" such as Cipher.getInstance("AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding") or EVP_*_ecb()
TLS/SSL configuration enables SSLv2, SSLv3, TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, RC4, DES, 3DES, MD5, or SHA1 cipher suites
RSA encryption uses Cipher.getInstance("RSA/ECB/PKCS1Padding") or RSA_public_encrypt(..., RSA_PKCS1_PADDING) instead of OAEP
Custom encryption/hash code uses XOR, shifts, rotations, LFSR, lookup tables, or proprietary encrypt()/decrypt()/hash() without a vetted crypto library
negative_signals: AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, SHA-256/SHA-384/SHA-512, SHA-3, or HMAC-SHA-256 from a vetted library
Password storage uses Argon2, bcrypt, scrypt, or PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 with salt and iteration/work factor
RSA encryption uses OAEP such as OAEPWithSHA-256AndMGF1Padding or RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING
Legacy MD5/SHA1 appears only in non-security checksums, cache keys, deduplication, or tests with no trust decision
TLS configuration disables SSLv2/SSLv3/TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1 and weak cipher suites
Algorithm choice is centralized behind a wrapper/provider and can be upgraded without changing callers
false_defense_traps: Keeping a proprietary algorithm secret; reverse engineering can expose it
Using MD5 or SHA1 only because the data is also encrypted elsewhere
Using AES but selecting ECB mode
Relying on old hardware crypto IP that cannot be patched when the algorithm becomes obsolete
verification_focus: Is the algorithm or protocol itself known-broken, obsolete, risky, non-standard, or private, rather than merely using weak parameters?

consequence_chains.trigger: MD5, SHA1, or MD4 is used for integrity, signature, certificate, or trust comparison
consequence_chains.consequence: Collision or preimage attacks enable forged data or spoofed identity

consequence_chains.trigger: RSA encryption is used without OAEP padding
consequence_chains.consequence: Chosen-ciphertext or padding attacks can expose encrypted data

consequence_chains.trigger: Fast hash such as MD5, SHA1, or SHA256 is used directly for password storage

patch_principle: Replace broken algorithms and protocols with currently vetted standards from maintained libraries
Do not design private or custom cryptographic algorithms
Use algorithm-appropriate modes and padding such as AEAD for encryption and OAEP for RSA
Review algorithms periodically and design crypto-agility through wrappers or provider configuration
Protect keys and do not skip required cryptographic steps
